entities.summary: The {piptm} package is the computation engine for the PIP Table Maker. Before implementing any code, we needed to clarify the data flow from {pipdata}'s clean survey datasets through Arrow partitions to {piptm}'s measure computations. Key decisions were needed around partition layout, manifest design, validation strategy, and how breakdown dimensions are handled.
entities.title: Data Pipeline Architecture — Ingestion, Manifest, and Computation Design

entities.summary: Before implementing the computation engine, we needed to design the most efficient strategy for computing Foster-Greer-Thorbecke (FGT) poverty measures. These are the core poverty indicators: headcount (α=0), poverty gap (α=1), and poverty severity (α=2). The design must handle multiple poverty lines, multiple breakdown dimensions (cross-tabulated), and integrate cleanly with the broader measure orchestrator.
entities.title: Efficient FGT Poverty Measure Computation Design

entities.summary: The original data pipeline architecture brainstorm (2026-03-16) established a Manifest-First with Lazy Validation approach where a single release manifest is loaded at startup. This follow-up brainstorm addresses the need to support **multiple PIP releases simultaneously**, since users may want to query results from different releases for reproducibility.
entities.title: Multi-Release Manifest Architecture

entities.summary: The `prepare_for_arrow()` pipeline in `{pipdata}` now injects a `version` column (e.g. `"v01_v04"`, derived from `metadata$vermast` and `metadata$veralt`) into every survey data.table. Currently this column is stored inside the Parquet file but is **not** used for partitioning.
entities.title: Version as partition key with manifest-based resolution

entities.summary: The March 17 brainstorm established the multi-release manifest architecture. Since then, the Arrow dataset partition layout has evolved: `version` is now a **partition variable** (subfolder) rather than being encoded in filenames. This changes how manifests are generated and how `{piptm}` loads data.
entities.title: Manifest Generation and Version Partition Filtering

entities.summary: With Phase 0 (Arrow dataset generation, manifest system, data loading) largely in place, the project needs to design the computation engine that takes partitioned survey microdata as input and produces poverty, inequality, and welfare statistics disaggregated across available dimensions.
entities.title: Computation Engine Design — Family-Based Orchestrator

entities.summary: The computation engine plan (Step 7, `table_maker()`) originally specified a strict dimension pre-filter: surveys missing **any** requested `by` dimension are dropped entirely before loading. This was deemed too strict — it silently excludes surveys that have partial dimension coverage, losing data unnecessarily.
entities.title: Dimension Pre-Filter: Partial Match with NA Fill

entities.summary: The Step 7 plan defines `table_maker(country_code, year, welfare_type, ...)` with three separate vectors. Filtering the manifest via `country_code %in% .cc & year %in% .yr & welfare_type == .wt` produces a **Cartesian product** — requesting COL-2010 and BOL-2000 would also match COL-2000 and BOL-2010 if they exist. Users specify **exact tuples**, not independent filters. Additionally, `welfare_type` is a scalar in the plan but users may request mixed welfare types across surveys (e.g., COL-2010-INC + BOL-2000-CON).
entities.title: table_maker() Input Parameter Structure

entities.summary: Step 8 of the computation engine plan (`2026-04-07-computation-engine.md`) proposes a per-slice vs grouped benchmark but is overengineered — it requires building a full alternative prototype just for comparison, uses an arbitrary 2× decision threshold, and may be answering the wrong question if I/O dominates runtime.
entities.title: Orchestration Strategy Benchmark — Per-Slice vs Grouped vs nthreads

entities.summary: <!-- Valid status values: decided, in-progress, abandoned -->
entities.title: Arrow vs Collapse End-to-End Benchmark

entities.summary: The computation engine (`table_maker()`) is complete and optimised. The next step is a Plumber-based API service layer that connects the PIP platform UI to the engine. The existing brainstorm (`2026-04-27-table-maker-input-parameters.md`) defined the `/table` and `/lookup` endpoint signatures and URL patterns. This brainstorm expands that to the full API surface.
entities.title: API Service Architecture for Table Maker

entities.summary: Benchmarking (50-iteration resample, 15 surveys over UNC share) showed that loading only the 6 needed columns instead of all 14 reduces Arrow I/O time from 1.658s to 0.524s — a **68% improvement**. Currently `load_surveys()` always loads all columns and `table_maker()` uses only what it needs.
entities.title: Column pruning in load_surveys() for table_maker performance

entities.summary: `compute_inequality()` sorts data by welfare within each group before computing Gini. However, the upstream data pipeline guarantees welfare-sorted row order:
entities.title: Remove redundant welfare sort in compute_inequality()

entities.summary: Need to add two new measures to the computation engine: - `obs_share` — proportion of total survey observations in each cross-tabulated cell - `pop_share` — proportion of total weighted survey population in each cell
entities.title: Cell observation share and population share measures

entities.summary: After adding `pop_share` and `obs_share` measures, we need a configurable suppression rule: if a cell's population share falls below a threshold, all other measures (except `pop_share` and `obs_share`) for that cell should be dropped from the output, with a warning explaining what was suppressed.
entities.title: Pop share threshold suppression for small cells

entities.summary: Follow-up to `2026-06-01-pop-share-threshold-suppression.md`.  That brainstorm implemented `pop_share_threshold` as a post-processing step in `table_maker()` Step 10.  However the implementation gated activation on `"pop_share" %in% measures`, making the safeguard accidentally opt-in: callers requesting only `"mean"` or `"gini"` by a dimension where one cell contains 0.2% of the survey receive unsuppressed results with no warning.
entities.title: Pop-share threshold as always-active suppression guard

entities.summary: Currently, deployment knowledge for the Table Maker API exists only in one person's head. The team needs this documented so anyone can deploy to DEV/QA/PROD environments. Deployment involves running three Azure DevOps pipelines in sequence, with some conditional logic about when to run the data copy pipeline.
entities.title: API Deployment Documentation

entities.summary: UI team requested endpoints to "store pip_ids" to support crash recovery / page refresh resilience. If a user is in Step 2 (variable selection) and the page refreshes or crashes, they would lose their Step 1 survey selections without some form of persistence.
entities.title: Session Storage Endpoints for Survey Selection Persistence

entities.summary: The ITS UI development team requested a way to persist survey selections from Step 1 (survey grid) so that if Step 2 (variable selection) crashes or refreshes, users don't lose their work.
entities.title: Survey-Specific Variable Filtering for Step 2

entities.summary: The user attached a comprehensive technical specification for a new `/description` endpoint that generates factual, dynamically constructed natural-language descriptions of tabular results produced by `table_maker()`. The goal was to stress-test the design, identify gaps, and confirm all requirements are properly set up before planning begins.

The team needs clear documentation to understand all available endpoints, their inputs and outputs, and how each endpoint maps to the UI steps and components.

entities.summary: `/table/download` (`inst/plumber/plumber.R:247-343`) is a stateless `POST` endpoint that converts an already-computed `/table` result into a downloadable CSV or RDS file without touching Arrow or recomputing via `table_maker()`. Previously, `/table` returned a flat long-format array of row objects, and `/table/download` simply ran `data.table::rbindlist(body$data, fill = TRUE)` and wrote the result out.
entities.title: /table/download input & output shape under Approach C

entities.summary: Implement the data preparation pipeline that takes clean survey datasets produced by {pipdata} (`.qs2` files) and generates validated, schema-consistent, partitioned Parquet datasets in the Master Arrow Repository. This work is a prerequisite for all downstream {piptm} functionality (manifest generation, data loading, and measure computation).
entities.title: Arrow Data Preparation Pipeline

entities.summary: Add `version` (e.g. `"v01_v04"`) as a 4th Hive partition key in the Arrow repository so that multiple survey versions coexist on disk. The release manifest's `file_path` field becomes the sole version-resolution mechanism for `{piptm}`. Also update the schema contract to replace the single `education` column with the original `educat4`, `educat5`, `educat7` columns preserved as-is from GMD data.
entities.title: Version as partition key with manifest-based resolution

entities.summary: Transition the manifest from storing physical `file_path` per entry to storing four logical partition filter keys (`country_code`, `year`, `welfare_type`, `version`). Update `{pipdata}` manifest generation to use the release inventory as the authoritative source, add dimension introspection, and produce the new JSON schema. Update `{piptm}` manifest loading and data access to use `open_dataset() |> filter()` with partition pushdown instead of `read_parquet(file_path)`.
entities.title: Manifest Generation and Version Partition Filtering

entities.summary: Implement the core computation engine for {piptm}: a family-based measure orchestrator that computes indicators across three families (poverty, inequality, welfare) and disaggregation dimensions, returning long-format results ready for JSON serialization. The engine must be fast, correct, and cleanly integrated with the existing manifest → load pipeline.anifest → load pipeline.
entities.title: Computation Engine — Family-Based Orchestrator

entities.summary: Create a standalone benchmark script that compares orchestration strategies for `table_maker()`'s per-survey computation loop, measures I/O vs compute time separately, and determines whether the current per-slice `lapply()` approach should be kept or replaced. This plan supersedes Step 8 of the computation engine plan (`2026-04-07-computation-engine.md`).
entities.title: Orchestration Strategy Benchmark

entities.summary: Replace the per-survey `lapply()` loop in `table_maker()` (Steps 6–7) with Approach B's grouped collapse strategy: build a single compound `GRP(c("pip_id", by))` across the full batch and dispatch directly to family functions. This eliminates 15× repeated GRP construction, dispatch overhead, and thread-lock acquisition, yielding a 72% speedup (0.12s vs 0.43s) as demonstrated by the orchestration benchmark.
entities.title: Refactor table_maker() to Approach B — Grouped Collapse Orchestration

entities.summary: Measure whether pushing column selection, filtering, or partial aggregation into Arrow (before `collect()`) speeds up the current collapse-based pipeline enough to justify the added complexity. The benchmark produces a data-driven recommendation with clear thresholds.
entities.title: Arrow vs Collapse End-to-End Benchmark

entities.summary: Implement a Plumber-based API service that exposes `table_maker()` and supporting discovery functions to the PIP platform UI and public consumers. Eight thin endpoints, a structured response envelope, and a global error handler — all delegating to existing tested {piptm} functions.
entities.title: API Service Layer — Plumber Endpoints

entities.summary: Implement a Plumber-based API service that exposes `table_maker()` and supporting discovery functions to the PIP platform UI and public consumers. Eight thin endpoints, a structured response envelope, and a global error handler — all delegating to existing tested {piptm} functions.

entities.summary: Benchmarking showed loading only needed columns instead of all 14 gives a 68% I/O improvement (1.658s → 0.524s) over UNC share. The fix is to add a `cols` parameter to `load_surveys()` and pass the needed columns from `table_maker()`.
entities.title: Column pruning in load_surveys() for table_maker performance

entities.summary: Add a single-entry-point `validate_parquet()` function to `R/validate_parquet.R` that dispatches to the three existing validators based on a `check` argument. Eliminates the need for callers to pick the right low-level function.

entities.summary: Refactor `load_surveys()` to assume all entries carry `welfare_vars` (new schema only). Remove all backward-compatibility handling for the retired single-`welfare` column schema.
entities.title: Remove legacy schema from load_surveys()

entities.summary: Change `table_maker()` so that surveys missing *any* requested breakdown dimension are skipped entirely (not loaded), rather than loaded with the missing dimension filled as NA.
entities.title: Dimension filter: skip partial-match surveys

entities.summary: Remove the `ppp_sort` inference/fallback mechanism from both `load_survey_microdata()` and `load_surveys()`. Default `ppp` to `2021L` (configurable via the argument default). In `load_surveys()`, when a survey lacks the welfare column for the requested PPP, skip that survey with a warning instead of erroring — return the remaining surveys that do have it.
entities.title: Refactor PPP handling: default to 2021, skip surveys missing welfare column

entities.summary: Remove `pip_measures()` and replace it with `pip_tablemaker_measures()` — a richer, static catalogue of analysis variables for the Table Maker Step 2 UI.  Update the GET `/measures` plumber endpoint to serve the new catalogue.  Update all affected tests.

entities.summary: - Use `piptm_manifest()` and variable registry to assemble UI rows.

entities.summary: Implement a release-specific variable registry that acts as the single source of truth for all variable-level metadata in the Table Maker system. The registry powers three plumber API metadata endpoints consumed by the Step 2 wizard UI. Remove the outdated static `pip_tablemaker_categories()` and `pip_tablemaker_covariates()` functions and replace them with registry-backed accessors.

entities.summary: Add a `filter_base` feature that restricts the sample entering computation by filtering microdata in the loading path only (API endpoint → `table_maker()` → `load_surveys()`), with Arrow-side filtering applied before `collect()`.

entities.summary: Refactor the piptm computation engine and Plumber API to support multiple analysis variables (not just welfare) while maintaining backward compatibility with existing tests and architectural patterns. The refactor introduces a variable type system (`welfare`, `poverty`, `continuous`, `binary`) that routes requests to appropriate computation families (`summary_stats`, `inequality`, `poverty`, `shares`). All changes prioritize correctness (the specification takes precedence over existing code) and maintain the deterministic, reproducible outputs expected by downstream PIP platform consumers.
entities.title: Table Endpoint & Computation Layer Refactor — Multi-Analysis-Variable Support

entities.summary: Bring `tests/testthat` in sync with the current implementation in `R/` for exported functions, treating current function code as ground truth.

The endpoint serves Step 3 of the PIP UI experience, providing researchers, economists, and data scientists with a human-readable overview of table contents, provenance, input specifications, execution details, and cell definitions.

entities.summary: Create a single Markdown file (`docs/api-contract.md`) documenting all 15 Table Maker API endpoints with OpenAPI-style schemas, inline UI mapping, structured response envelopes, error handling, and input validation rules. This serves as the internal handoff document for the UI/IT team to build against the existing API.

entities.summary: Add an HTML rendering option to the `/description` endpoint (inline styles only, all dynamic content escaped), selectable via a `format` field in the JSON request body that defaults to the current Markdown behavior; and fix awkward auto-generated sentence wording in the description model's templates before building the HTML renderer, so neither output format carries forward known poor phrasing.

entities.summary: **Outcome**: The description endpoint's layout section shows both the count and the category labels for each "by" dimension. Example: `gender` currently renders as `2` under Categories; after this change it renders as `2: male, female`. `pov_status` renders as `2: poor, non-poor`.

entities.summary: Replace the abstract "this cell" / "total weighted survey population" plain-meaning templates for the three share measures (`pop_share`, `target_within_group_share`, `target_survey_share`) in `build_cell_definition()` with concrete "Among X, what fraction..." phrasing built from the actual filter clause, group label, and target-variable label already used elsewhere in the description, while keeping an honest, simple statement for the `pop_share` degenerate case (`by = NULL`).
entities.title: Rework plain-meaning wording for share measures

entities.summary: Replace ambiguous prose for `pop_share`, `target_within_group_share`, and `target_survey_share` in the `/description` endpoint's Cell Definition section with a structured four-column table: Measure, Denominator, Numerator, and Plain meaning. Render the table in Markdown and HTML while preserving existing non-share behavior.
entities.title: Structured Cell Definition table for share measures (revised)

entities.summary: Replace the ambiguous, near-identical prose sentences generated for the three share measures (`pop_share`, `target_within_group_share`, `target_survey_share`) in the `/description` endpoint's Cell Definition section with a structured four-column table (Measure, Denominator, Numerator, Plain meaning), rendered in both Markdown and HTML, while leaving non-share measures and all other description sections unchanged.

entities.summary: Replace row-dropping suppression in `table_maker()` with cell-level NR masking at a 0.1% default threshold, remove the `population` column, and format the main `/table` API values as strings (x100 for proportion/Gini measures, 2 decimals, whole numbers for counts, `"NR"` for masked cells). Download and description changes are deferred to a follow-up plan.
entities.title: Population share threshold: NR masking and API value formatting

entities.summary: Replace the repeatable `by` parameter on `/table` with four named slot parameters — `column`, `row`, `superColumn`, `superRow` — each accepting exactly one variable name. Assemble them into an ordered `by` vector inside `validate_table_input()`. Migrate the `/description` fallback to the same parameters in the same change.
entities.title: /table explicit slot parameters replacing ordered by (revised)

entities.summary: Replace the single repeatable `by` parameter on `/table` with four explicit, named slot parameters - `column`, `row`, `superColumn`, `superRow` - each accepting exactly one variable name. Assembly back into an ordered `by` vector happens in `validate_table_input()` at the API boundary.
entities.title: /table explicit slot parameters replacing ordered by

entities.summary: Update `POST /table/download` so it accepts the **Approach C** `data[]` payload returned by `/table` (per-survey objects with `layout` + `cells[]`) and statelessly flattens it into a rectangular **Shape A** table (one row per observed cell, measures as columns) before exporting as CSV or RDS. Reject legacy flat-row payloads and malformed inputs with HTTP `400` in the standard JSON error envelope (replacing the temporary HTTP `500` characterization behavior).
entities.title: /table/download Approach C stateless flattening (Shape A)

entities.summary: Reshape the `/table` response (with `include_metadata` off) from flat long-format rows into **Approach C**: `data[]` holds one object per survey, each carrying header fields, a `layout` block (fixed keys `columns`, `rows`, `superColumns`, `superRows`; `null` for unused slots) and a `cells[]` array of the **observed** (computed/masked) cells. Every cell carries all four fixed slot keys (`superRow`, `row`, `superColumn`, `column`, each `{code, label}` or `null`) and a `measures` object keyed by measure name. Category order in `layout` and cell order in `cells[]` are deterministic and registry-sourced.
entities.title: /table response format: layout + observed cells[] (Approach C)

entities.summary: A new binary download endpoint (`POST /table/download`) was added to convert already-computed `/table` rows into CSV or RDS. Two reliability issues appeared during hardening: 1. Some malformed JSON request bodies could reach plumber/parser failure paths and return HTTP 500 instead of the endpoint's expected JSON error envelope with HTTP 400. 2. The size cap (`25 MB`) was enforced only via `Content-Length`, so requests with missing/invalid headers could still parse oversized bodies in memory. Symptoms: - Inconsistent error behavior for invalid payloads. - Risk of memory pressure if a large body is accepted without a trustworthy header.
entities.title: POST /table/download malformed JSON 500s and size-guard bypass

entities.summary: While manually verifying `POST /table/download` against a live, running API (not just `pr$call()` unit tests), two defects surfaced that unit tests had not caught: 1. **Duplicate `Content-Type` header** on every response (success and error). Raw HTTP output looked like: ``` Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8 Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="table.csv" Content-Type: application/octet-stream ``` Two `Content-Type` headers in one response is technically invalid HTTP and risky for client parsers that read only the last/first value inconsistently. 2. **Swagger/OpenAPI misrepresented the request body.** `pr$getApiSpec()$paths[["/table/download"]][["post"]]` showed: ```r requestBody present: FALSE parameters count: 1 # name="body", in="query", type="string" ``` Swagger UI would have rendered `body` as a string...
entities.title: POST /table/download: serializer-induced duplicate Content-Type and Swagger body-as-query-param

entities.summary: While implementing cell-level `NR` masking and API value formatting for `table_maker()`/`format_table_output()` (plan: `.cg-docs/plans/2026-10-20-pop-share-nr-masking.md`), a `data-risk` review surfaced a P0 finding in a completely different, unmodified-by-this-plan endpoint: `POST /table/download`. `/table/download` is designed to accept rows "typically copied from the `/table` response" (per `docs/api-contract.md`) and convert them to CSV/RDS. Before this session's work, `/table`'s `value` field was always a raw numeric. After this session's work, `/table`'s `value` field became a **formatted character string**: scaled-and-rounded percentages (e.g. `"45.67"`), whole-number counts, or the literal sentinel `"NR"` for masked (disclosure-controlled) cells. `/table/download`'s existing code did: `as.numeric("NR")` silently returns `NA` — indistinguishable from genuine missing data,...
entities.title: /table/download silently corrupts data when a sibling endpoint's output format changes

But a standalone, minimal reproduction of the grouping step alone (in an isolated script, same data.table version) worked fine with an **unnamed** character vector of the same values. The failure only reproduced when the...
entities.title: data.table by= silently uses names(), not values(), of a named character vector

entities.summary: The `/table` endpoint changed from flat rows to Approach C payloads: each survey contains header metadata, a four-slot `layout`, and dense `cells[]` objects whose measure values are already formatted display strings. The `POST /table/download` endpoint still expected flat rows and used `rbindlist()` directly on `body$data`, causing nested payloads to fail. The boundary also had several malformed-input hazards: - `null` or empty scalar header fields could produce raw R indexing errors; - malformed `surveyid_year` or `poverty_line` values could silently become `NA` through coercion; - duplicate or colliding dimension/measure names could silently overwrite output columns; - malformed active cell slots could be...
entities.title: POST /table/download Approach C flattening and boundary validation

entities.summary: The `{piptm}` pipeline relies on a **pre-sort contract**: welfare values in each survey's microdata are sorted ascending before `compute_inequality()` is called. `compute_inequality()` was refactored to remove its internal `setorder()`, trusting this contract entirely. The contract holds when each partition directory contains exactly one Parquet file — the `{pipdata}` pipeline writes exactly one file per partition under normal operation. However, if a partition directory were to contain two files (retried write, manual copy, pipeline shard, test artefact), `open_dataset()` on that directory concatenates the files in file-system order. The result is: `compute_inequality()` receives this combined vector, the `is.unsorted()` guard fires only on...
entities.title: Arrow open_dataset on multiple Parquet files silently breaks within-survey welfare sort

entities.summary: `compute_inequality()` calls `collapse::fsum()`, `collapse::fcumsum()`, and `collapse::fmean()` on `welfare` and `weight` vectors. When either vector contains `NA`, the functions silently exclude those rows from all calculations because `collapse` defaults to `na.rm = TRUE` everywhere. The visible symptom is wrong — but numerically plausible — Gini and MLD values. No error, no warning. The bias is proportional to the share of NA rows and their welfare values. On a survey with 0.5% NA rows near the top of the distribution the Gini can be understated by ~0.01 without any diagnostic signal.
entities.title: collapse::fsum/fcumsum silently drops NA rows, biasing weighted statistics

entities.summary: When new optional columns are added to the PIP Arrow schema (e.g. household size, infrastructure indicators, labour variables), the pipeline raises false "extra column" errors like: This happens even when the column is genuinely schema-conformant, because the new name was added to `pip_arrow_schema()` but not propagated to every allow-list that enforces it.

entities.summary: An API endpoint accepting `description_metadata` from JSON crashed with malformed inputs because: 1. Code assumed `data.table` structures but `jsonlite::fromJSON()` returns `data.frame` 2. Empty data.tables became `list()` (not `NULL` or empty `data.frame`) 3. List-column elements could be `NULL`, integers, or wrong types after deserialization 4. Missing columns weren't validated before access **Symptoms**: - Silent crashes: `loaded$country_code` on `NULL` → error - Type errors: `vapply()` over `NULL` elements in list-column → `character(0)` violates contract - Malformed data passed schema checks → downstream crashes **Impact**: P0 data corruption / crash risk when JSON metadata bypasses validation. ---
entities.title: JSON Round-Trip Defensive Coding: Schema Validation + Test Coverage Strategy

entities.summary: The `table_maker()` pipeline was meeting a 3s compute target in isolation but its real-world performance was unknown when I/O (network reads from a UNC share) was included. Multiple optimization ideas existed (column pruning, Arrow aggregation push-down, Arrow pre-sort) but none had been measured. ---
entities.title: Arrow I/O and Compute Strategy: Lessons from Benchmarking

entities.summary: `load_surveys()` always called `open_dataset() |> collect()` without any `select()`, loading all 14 schema columns into memory. `table_maker()` then used only the handful it needed (welfare, weight, by-dimensions). The unused columns were transferred over the UNC network share but immediately discarded. Benchmark result (50-iteration resample, 15 surveys): - All 14 columns: **1.658s** median I/O - 6 needed columns: **0.524s** median — **68% faster**
entities.title: Column Pruning in load_surveys(): Implementation Pattern

entities.summary: Testing a plumber API without a running HTTP server is non-trivial. Three concrete issues emerged when writing integration tests for the `{piptm}` plumber endpoints: 1. **Plumber crashes (500) instead of returning 400** when a required function parameter (no default) is absent from the query string — the error fires _before_ the handler body runs, bypassing `validate_*()` → `api_error()`. 2. **`pr$errorHandler` is not a public field** in plumber ≥ 1.3.x. Tests that check `is.function(pr$errorHandler)` fail with `FALSE`; the error handler is stored in a private R5 field. 3. **`jsonlite` serializes empty character vectors and `NULL` differently depending on context.** `character(0)` in...
entities.title: Programmatic plumber endpoint testing with pr$call() and Hive fixtures

entities.summary: `compute_inequality()` was refactored to remove its internal `setorder()` call, relying instead on a documented pre-sort contract: callers must supply welfare data sorted ascending. All existing tests passed — but none of them would have caught a regression where the upstream pipeline stopped sorting welfare. If `pipdata::generate_arrow_dataset()` ever dropped its sort, `load_surveys()` would return unsorted data, and `compute_inequality()` would produce silently wrong Gini values with every existing test still green.
entities.title: Testing pre-sort contracts: verify the contract is required, not just that it holds
